value.hook: before touching the TLS front (tls-front.ts, prod-https/dev-https), bootstrap cookies, Origin allowlists, or adding any CG_* environment variable
value.title: HTTPS front, cookies over two protocols, and CG_* env names

sections.name: body
sections.value:
- The TLS front (apps/web/src/lib/tls-front.ts) is trusted by Next ONLY via a per-launch secret
  (CHAINGLASS_FRONT_SECRET, header x-chainglass-front) from a loopback peer; socket-peer.ts deletes it from
  process.env at install, and the sidecar runs with `env -u`. Never trust XFF/X-Forwarded-Proto without it;
  test with spoofed XFF/Host/marker from the LAN (a curl matrix is the proof the prime asks for).
- Use requestClient() (address + secure) for rate-limit keys and cookie Secure, never NODE_ENV or the raw
  socket; unmap ::ffff: IPv4 or one client gets two rate-limit buckets.
- Cookies ignore ports, and Chrome won't let http overwrite a Secure cookie of the same name/host. HTTPS uses
  a separate name (__Secure-chainglass-bootstrap); read it through readBootstrapCookie everywhere (cookie
  gate, BootstrapGate, local-auth, terminal/remote-view token routes, repo-info). Prove http AFTER https in
  the same browser.
- Origin allowlist env vars (TERMINAL_WS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS, CG_REMOTE_VIEW__ALLOWED_ORIGINS) REPLACE the
  defaults, so the recipes compute default + https://<cert name>:HTTPS_PORT (`tls-front.ts origins ...`).
  streamd inherits Next's env.
- Until B9, env.parser rejected any CG_* name with a single underscore inside a segment (CG_SERVER_PORT,
  CG_REMOTE_VIEW__DAEMON_PORT): Next/CLI config load threw → 500s. The B9 fix allows them; if you see
  "Invalid segment", fix the parser, don't invent a non-CG_ alias (I did once; B9 reverted it). Any env
  var you add for a Next-spawned child must be in turbo.json dev passThroughEnv too.
- The managed headless browser never runs rAF/ResizeObserver; prove terminal resize at the WS protocol
  level. The first resize message never applies on any transport (known), the second does.
- The edit tool's relative paths resolve to the MAIN tree; use absolute worktree paths always.
